newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq ready to improve ties with Iran if POWs freed.
newsitem.headline: Iraq ready to improve ties with Iran if POWs freed.

text.p: Iraq said on Saturday it was ready to improve relations with Iran if Tehran freed thousands of Iraqi prisoners of war from the 1980-88 war between the two nations and returned Iraqi aircraft.
"Iraq is ready to open a new page with Iran after the release of (Iraqi) prisoners of war ... "Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel said in a frontpage editorial.

Iraqi President Saddam Hussein on Friday marked the anniversary of the end of the war by demanding that new Iranian President Mohammad Khatami free the POWs and return Iraqi civil and military planes which fled to Iran to avoid bombing at the start of the 1991 Gulf war over Kuwait.
According to the International Committee of the Red Cross, more than 13,000 Iraqi POWs have not been repatriated. Iraq says the number exceeds 20,000. Iran denies it has any Iraqi prisoners.
The government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said the new Iranain government should show its goodwill towards Iraq by returning the prisoners and the planes.
"If Iran fulfills these steps, it will be a positive beginning which will allow the establishment of new relations," the newspaper said.
The ball is in the Iranian court ... Will Iran seize the opportunity... and respond to Iraq's demands," Jumhouriya asked.
An Iraqi Foreign Ministry spokesman on Saturday accused Iran of blocking mail from Iraqi POWs to their families.

"Allowing only a very limited number of Iraqi POWs to send letters to their relatives out of thousands of prisoners ... aims at creating a state of unrest and confusion among their families," the spokesman was quoted by the Iraqi News Agency INA as saying.
